coverage.found: No search spent. Cremation is the norm in Bhutan, which makes this unlikely.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Vehicle registration renewal needs a fitness (road-worthiness) test and an emission test every year. Route permits are issued by the transport authority (now BCTA, formerly RSTA). No official route-permit renewal procedure found. Fleets are small.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Street vending is covered by K10. Money changers are licensed by the RMA under the Foreign Exchange Regulations 2013, but no 2025 rules or licensee list were found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools and institutes are licensed under BCTA rules (graduates get a shorter learner's-licence wait). Private ECCD centres are organised (50 centres in a 2024 association) but no registration regulation was found. BFDA food-business licensing is not documented in search. Pools are small.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Only 3 private POL distributors (Bhutan Oil, Druk Petroleum, Damchen) supply about 48 stations. Prices are set by the Department of Trade and margins are fixed. The pool is too small and there is no licensing detail.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: 122 cooperatives and 711 farmer groups (DAMC 2024, via ICA snapshot). The Cooperatives and Farmer Groups Bill 2025 was adopted by the Assembly in Dec 2025 and shifts registration to districts. Annual audited reports were required under the 2001 Act. Small pool, state-run.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: No search spent. Bhutan has free public healthcare, so insurer billing is probably minimal, but this is unverified.

coverage.found: Bhutan Medicine Rules and Regulation 2025 (PDF on oag.gov.bt) has Chapter VII, Technical Authorization for Sale and Distribution. The PDF fetch returned 503, so register duties were not read. A Jan 2026 BBS report shows embargoes for missing documents. Nothing new beyond K04.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Contractors must register with BCTA (class, owned equipment and staff minimums, insurance proofs) before getting a trade licence. Tenders require a valid CDB registration certificate, trade licence and tax clearance. Mines and quarries run on renewable 5-30 year tenures. Boulder and aggregate supply moved to open auction from April 2025 (Forest and Park Services). No DGM return forms found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Two searches failed to find Bhutan's AML/CFT DNFBP schedule. The FIU sits in or under the RMA. Reporting entities unverified.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Department of Tourism and GovTech built a free Tourist Registration System, launched 8 Aug 2025 and mandatory from 1 Sep 2025, for licensed hotels (passport, name, DOB, gender, check-in/out, daily entry). Village Homestay Guidelines were updated in Jan 2026 and Tourism Rules and Regulations 2024 replaced the 2022 rules. Hotel PMS vendors exist (Hotelogix, BookMyTour). No TRS integration API found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: BAFRA issues export and phytosanitary certificates. Since the March 2024 FSSAI-BFDA agreement, food exports to India (except milk) need a BFDA Health Certificate. No Bhutan-specific traceability rule found. Timber and fish not checked.

coverage.category: 31. Vehicle fitness and emission testing (country-specific)
coverage.found: Fitness and emission tests are mandatory at annual registration renewal. BCTA contracts a single emission-testing agent (Green Bhutan Services, 3-year contract, Aug 2026 report), and chassis-number verification is now mandatory. State-contracted monopoly, so no software buyer.

coverage.category: 32. BFDA food-business licensing and India export health certificates (country-specific)
coverage.found: Food Act 2005 requires a food safety licence (2017 report); BFDA health certificates for exports to India since 2024. Current licensing and renewal procedure not found.

coverage.category: 33. Outbound overseas employment agent licensing (country-specific)
coverage.found: Regulation on Employment of Bhutanese Overseas 2021 (Clause 88 fine Nu 600,000 for unlicensed recruitment); Bhutan Today reports fraudulent overseas recruitment agencies. Number of licensed agents unknown.

coverage.category: 34. Boulder, crusher and NRDCL aggregate supply (country-specific)
coverage.found: Cabinet guideline effective April 2025 puts boulder and dredging supply to open auction. Sarpang crusher operators complain about a royalty of Nu 4,000 per truck. No recurring return form found.

coverage.category: 35. Village homestay certification and operation (country-specific)
coverage.found: Department of Tourism Guidelines for Certification, Registration and Operation of Village Homestays 2026: assessment, certification, monitoring, non-commercialisation. A business licence is reportedly not required for homestays. Number of homestays unknown.

coverage.category: 36. Tourist Registration System for hotels (country-specific, Jan-Sep 2025 rule)
coverage.found: Mandatory daily guest entry for licensed hotels since 1 Sep 2025. Free state portal, so no add-on need unless a PMS connector is wanted.

coverage.category: 37. Authorised money changers and foreign exchange dealers (country-specific)
coverage.found: RMA Foreign Exchange Regulations 2013 include a chapter on authorised money changers. No 2025 update or licensee list found.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Since the Cabinet decision of Sept 2023, foreign domestic workers are legal as 'home-based personal care workers and child caregivers'. Employer needs Department of Labour approval first, then Department of Immigration work permit; contract signed at point of entry (ROICE) plus an undertaking letter; 3-year recruitment with annual permit renewal; tracked in the Foreign Workers Management System. 2025 guidelines: 8-hour day plus 2 hours paid overtime, weekly rest, employer pays transport, insurance and medical cover; minimum wage Nu 3,750 per month; Department of Labour does home inspections. Only about 600 workers were approved Jan 2023 to Oct 2025 (Kuensel via ANN, Jan 2026), and agents mostly just process permits. The household base is tiny. Sources: https://asianews.network/foreign-domestic-workers-lift-burden-off-bhutanese-working-moms ; https://thebhutanese.bt/foreign-domestic-workers-now-allowed-for-the-elderly-sick-and-disabled-too/ . Related to K03 (work-permit renewal desk).

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No second-hand dealer or pawnbroker regime found. Only general retail and wholesale trade licences (Retail Trade Regulation 2006, licence valid 1 year, renewal needs a Tax Clearance Certificate from the Regional Trade and Industry Office). Nothing sector-specific. Sources: https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/bt/national-legislation/bhutan-retail-trade-regulation-2006 ; https://wikiprocedure.com/index.php/Bhutan_-_Renew_Your_Retail_or_Wholesale_Trade_License (unofficial wiki).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Two searches found no text of Bhutan's AML/CFT law and no list of DNFBPs. Only a Thimphu law-firm marketing page says the RMA supervises banks and the FIU handles suspicious transaction reports, and that 'certain DNFBPs' are covered. Unverified whether jewellers are reporting entities. Mark as unverified; the RMA/FIU site and the APG mutual evaluation were not reached. Source: https://lawzana.com/aml-compliance-lawyers/thimphu

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler licence or parts-dealer register found. BBS reports no clear policy for disposal of scrapped and deregistered vehicles (responsibility falls on individuals), and Thimphu Thromde says Environmental Clearance is not required for the Olarongchhu auto-scrap site. RICB sells insured wrecks through salvage tenders in Phuentsholing. Unregulated sector, so no recurring duty. Sources: https://www.bbs.bt/228480/ ; https://www.ricb.bt/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/PMB-AUCTION-NOTICE-RICB-1.pdf . Related to K10 only in spirit.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper registration or reporting duty found. Beekeeping is promoted by the Department of Livestock and ICIMOD, with voluntary groups (Beekeepers' Cooperative of Bhutan, 104 members; Bumthang association). Tiny base with no mandatory register. Sources: https://dialogue.earth/en/nature/why-are-honeybees-dying-in-bhutan/ ; https://icimod.org/bees-boost-business-for-bhutans-farmers

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Act 2011 and Water Regulations (2012, a 2014 version is also listed) require an Environmental Clearance or permit from the National Environment Commission for water abstraction (art.44 per UNEP LEAP); groundwater abstraction is permitted only where there is no surface alternative (art.63). No driller licence or driller register found. Applicants are mainly hydropower, industry and utilities, not quiet small firms. Sources: https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/bt/national-legislation/water-regulation-bhutan-2014 ; https://www.informea.org/en/legislation/water-act-bhutan-2011

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Waste Prevention and Management Act 2009 and Regulation 2012 (NEC apex; Thromdes and Dzongkhags implement; service fees differ for households, commercial and corporate users). No desludging or hauler licence register found. Thimphu sewerage master plan relies on septic tanks and soak pits for unconnected households. Nothing new beyond the general NEC waste regulation. Sources: https://indiaenvironmentportal.org.in/reports-and-documents/bhutan-waste-prevention-and-management-regulation-2012 ; https://thebhutanese.bt/lyonpo-says-his-wife-scolds-him-over-thimphus-sewage-system/

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: One search found no Bhutan lift, boiler or pressure-vessel inspection rule. Only the Labour and Employment Act 2007 and the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2012 (Department of Labour) as the general OSH framework, with no equipment-specific provisions confirmed. Unverified; the OSH Regulations text was not opened. Source: https://rivermate.com/guides/bhutan/health-and-safety (commercial guide). Very few lifts exist anyway.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Bhutan Drinking Water Quality Standard 2016 (under the Water Act 2011) applies to all supplies including those run by water user associations, institutions and households, and requires monitoring, water safety plans, data management and reporting. Rural Water Safety Plan facilitator's guide exists (2013). Rural supplies are rarely tested (Public Health Laboratory 2012). Community schemes are state-supported and unpaid, so weak buyer. Sources: https://www.informea.org/ar/legislation/bhutan-drinking-water-quality-standard-2016 ; https://wsportal.org/resource/rural-water-safety-plan-rwsp-facilitators-guide/

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Cremation is the norm. The main Thimphu facility (Hejo crematorium) is on Zhung Dratshang land with a caretaker; cremation is free apart from firewood (Nu 2,700); a local paper says no professional funeral service industry exists (one 2016 directory listing contradicts this). No licensing regime found. Sources: https://thebhutanese.bt/?p=27860 ; https://thebhutanese.bt/lack-of-crematory-space-an-issue-for-the-people/

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Nothing on miller or grain-trader licensing or BAFRA warehouse rules. Food Corporation of Bhutan Ltd (state-owned) dominates grain: 25 district warehouses, 8,613 MT mandated rice reserve, sells to private retailers at wholesale rates, 19,897 MT sold in 2025. Private commodity trade is thin, and the main buyer is a state-owned enterprise. Source: https://fcbl.bt/hr/report/Annual%20Report%202025.pdf . Coffee/cocoa not searched.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Healthcare Services Rules and Regulations 2025, Section 47: no one may operate a healthcare centre without MoH technical authorisation. MoH gave unlicensed private operators a one-year grace period from about May 2025 (so roughly May 2026, extension unverified). Article says no licence had been issued to private centres so far. Public healthcare is free; RICB's cashless medical insurance (launched 1 July 2024) targets treatment at 500+ hospitals in India, with low uptake. No evidence that domestic private clinics bill insurers. Sources: https://thebhutanese.bt/moh-issues-a-one-year-deadline-notification-to-shut-down-unlicensed-private-healthcare-centers/ ; https://asianews.network/bhutans-health-ministry-warns-against-unlicensed-private-clinics/ ; https://www.bbs.bt/?p=233282

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Guidelines for Private Security Firms and Private Security Personnel 2016 (Ministry of Home and Cultural Affairs, approved by Lhengye Zhungtshog); 2016 reporting named two licensed firms. A 2026 ANN report finds guards on 12-hour shifts at wages below the Nu 400 minimum daily wage, and a Department of Labour inspection drive has started. Tenders (RICB, UNDP) require a valid trade licence and labour-law-compliant pay. No manpower-supplier register found. Small number of firms. Sources: https://www.moha.gov.bt/?p=851 ; https://asianews.network/?p=295111 ; https://www.ricb.bt/?p=11848
